criteria.observation: Asked a scoping question before answering. Proposed diagnosing why earlier pilots failed before building anything, and tied any budget request to a measured baseline on one process with a named owner.

evidence.quote: Can I ask one thing first: how big is the company, roughly?
I'd want to spend the first two weeks finding out why the pilots didn't stick.
We measured it for two cycles before building anything

gaps: Did not say how they would choose between candidate processes beyond "a clear cost".

criteria.observation: Declined to invent an ROI figure, named a gap in their own answer on contracts, and described a past mistake as their own.

evidence.quote: I can't give you a credible number without your data
I don't have a full answer on the contract side.
That was my miss, I hadn't tested it in the field.

criteria.observation: Described leading a scheduling-tool rollout, the wrong first fix (more training), the field visit that found the cause, and the changes made. Was specific about which decision was shared.

evidence.quote: Adoption was about thirty percent after six weeks.
Adoption got to about seventy percent over the next two months.
It was a joint call. I proposed it, but the ops lead had to sign off

gaps: Adoption figures are self-reported; how they were measured was not discussed.
The candidate's own role in the invoice reconciliation example was not stated.

criteria.observation: Answered each objection with a concrete mechanism rather than reassurance: end users in the design from week one, human approval on customer-facing output, a stop threshold agreed in advance, and early union involvement.

evidence.quote: I'd put the planners in the room from week one
the tool drafts and a named person approves
I'd want the union rep briefed before the pilot starts, not after.

gaps: When asked for a number, offered a method for getting one rather than a range or estimate.

uncertainties: The invoice reconciliation result (three days to under one day) was from "a previous client"; the candidate's role in it is unclear.
The risk answer was not followed up, so its depth was not tested.
readback: Before answering, you asked how big the company was.
You said you'd spend the first two weeks finding out why earlier AI pilots didn't stick, then start with one process that has a clear cost and an owner.
Asked for a dollar figure, you said you couldn't give a credible one without data, and described measuring a baseline before building.
On the failed forecasting pilot, you said the planners should be involved from week one and the output should land in the spreadsheet they already use.
On risk, you said a named person approves anything customer-facing, a stop threshold is agreed up front, and the union is briefed early. You said the contract side needs legal input.
You described a scheduling-tool rollout that went from about 30% to about 70% adoption after a field visit, an offline mode, and a shorter form, decided jointly with the ops lead.
